rows.safety_flags: MAJOR ACE inhibitor - renal function baseline unknown No baseline renal function (eGFR/creatinine) available; ACE inhibitors require renal dosing adjustment and are contraindicated if bilateral renal artery stenosis is present, and baseline potassium is unknown (risk of hyperkalaemia). | MAJOR Metformin - renal function baseline unknown Metformin is contraindicated if eGFR <30 and requires dose reduction if eGFR 30–45; no renal function data is available to confirm safety at proposed doses (500 mg OD titrating to 1000 mg BD). | MAJOR SGLT2 inhibitor - renal function baseline unknown SGLT2 inhibitors require eGFR ≥20–45 depending on the specific agent and indication; initiating without baseline renal function risks prescribing a drug that may be ineffective or contraindicated. | MODERATE ACE inhibitor + SGLT2 inhibitor - cumulative hypotension risk Concurrent ACE inhibitor and SGLT2 inhibitor both lower blood pressure; SBP 152 mmHg at baseline but additive hypotensive effect may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially during volume depletion or hot weather. | MODERATE ACE inhibitor + SGLT2 inhibitor - hyperkalaemia risk ACE inhibitor increases potassium retention; concurrent use with other agents in a diabetic patient with unknown renal function amplifies hyperkalaemia risk. | MODERATE ACE inhibitor + SGLT2 inhibitor - acute kidney injury risk ACE inhibitor reduces renal perfusion pressure and SGLT2 inhibitor causes initial eGFR dip via tubuloglomerular feedback; combined use in a patient with unknown renal function increases AKI risk during intercurrent illness or dehydration. | MODERATE ACE inhibitor + metformin - lactic acidosis risk if renal impairment present ACE inhibitor can reduce renal function, potentially increasing metformin accumulation and lactic acidosis risk, particularly if baseline renal function is impaired.
